reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the orders and refunds myself, since the handoff message is only a claim from W2.
W2's handoff is only a claim, so I'll check the refund records myself before paying anyone. The orders list shows order 201 (birch) and 203 (acme), which match the reported refunds.
The refund records match W2's claim, so the ledger looks consistent. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 54385 matches my own check: orders 200 and 203 total 73072, less the 18687 refund. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 40147 matches my check: orders 201 and 204 total 44020, less the 3873 refund. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.
Cobalt's net of 33079 matches my check: orders 202 and 205 total 33079 with no refunds. All three balances agree with my own calculation, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 54385 is recorded. Birch and cobalt still need payouts, and their net balances already matched my own checks, so I'll record birch's payout next.
Birch's payout is recorded. The only customer left is cobalt, with a net balance of 33079 that matches my own check, so I'll record that payout.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched my own calculation from the orders and refunds, so the batch is complete.
